FACT-1.gloss: Gretchen has a total of 110 coins

FACT-2.gloss: There are 30 more gold coins than silver coins

RULE-1.gloss: If a person has a total coin count of 110 and the gold coins equal the silver coins plus 30, then there exist silver and gold coin counts that satisfy the two sum equations
RULE-1.formula: ∀x((TotalCoins(x, n_110) ∧ GoldEqualsSilverPlus(x, n_30)) → ∃n_S ∃n_G(SilverCoins(x, n_S) ∧ GoldCoins(x, n_G) ∧ Plus(n_S, n_G, n_110) ∧ Plus(n_S, n_30, n_G)))

RULE-2.gloss: If silver and gold counts satisfy G+S=110 and G=S+30, then silver is 40 and gold is 70
RULE-2.formula: ∀x∀n_S∀n_G((SilverCoins(x, n_S) ∧ GoldCoins(x, n_G) ∧ Plus(n_S, n_G, n_110) ∧ Plus(n_S, n_30, n_G)) → SilverCoins(x, n_40) ∧ GoldCoins(x, n_70))

INF-1.gloss: Gretchen's silver and gold counts exist from TOTAL and relation by RULE-1
INF-1.formula: ∃n_S ∃n_G (SilverCoins(gretchen, n_S) ∧ GoldCoins(gretchen, n_G) ∧ Plus(n_S, n_G, n_110) ∧ Plus(n_S, n_30, n_G))

INF-2.gloss: From INF-1 and RULE-2 by Modus Ponens
